sources.note: Nothing for Bulusu. Bulusu appears only in ch. 11 'Southwest Sabah revisited' (pp. 359-360, 372, 393-394, 398 sec. 11.4.5) as a Murutic language of Kalimantan Timur and in functor/innovation tables (forms cited without accent marks). The only stress discussions are for Philippine languages (Manide/Alabat contrastive accent sec. 8.2.9; Maranao p. 287 fn. 3 'most languages native to Mindanao and areas further south have lost contrastive stress').

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid buru1304 and its bibliography (6 entries); Wikipedia id/en 'Bahasa Burusu'/'Burusu language'; Peta Bahasa (Kemendikdasmen) Kalimantan Utara/Timur pages; Garuda, Neliti, LoC catalog searches for Bulusu/Burusu/Berusu/Belusu
sources.note: No phonological description of Bulusu located anywhere: Glottolog has 0 grammar/phonology/sketch refs; Indonesian indexes return only ethnographic/folklore/education items on 'Dayak Bulusu/Belusu'; Peta Bahasa has no Bulusu entry; LoC has no Indonesian monograph on the language.

sources.note: Only modern published primary source with Bulusu data by a phonologically careful fieldworker; its introduction/transcription conventions may state whether stress is marked or predictable (penultimate) in the North Borneo languages including Bulusu. Wordlist-type work, so a stress statement is possible but not certain.
